title: と言うと — “speaking of ～ / if you say ～”
summary: Noun + と言うと takes up a topic and says what it makes the speaker think of or what usually comes to mind: “speaking of ～.” It is very close to と言えば. It can also ask for clarification: “if you mean ～.”

patterns.gloss: noun + と言うと (夏と言うと、秋と言うと)

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ と言うと、〜のことですか
patterns.gloss: noun + と言うと、…のことですか: do you mean ～?

body.p: With a noun, it is the image the word brings: 夏と言うと、海を思い出す. The second half often has 思い出す, 思い浮かべる, やはり, or a general comment on the topic.
They are mostly interchangeable. と言うと highlights the association with the word itself; と言えば often shifts the conversation to a related topic. The nuance is small.
In conversation, と言うと can also check what the other person means. 田中さんと言うと、あの背の高い人ですか (Tanaka... do you mean the tall man?).

examples.ja: 夏（なつ）と言（い）うと、海（うみ）を思（おも）い出（だ）す。
examples.romaji: Natsu to iu to, umi o omoidasu.
examples.tr: When you say summer, I think of the sea.

examples.ja: 京都（きょうと）と言（い）うと、古（ふる）いお寺（てら）を思（おも）い浮（う）かべる。
examples.romaji: Kyōto to iu to, furui otera o omoiukaberu.
examples.tr: Speaking of Kyoto, I picture its old temples.

examples.ja: 秋（あき）と言（い）うと、やはり紅葉（こうよう）が一番（いちばん）美（うつく）しい。
examples.romaji: Aki to iu to, yahari kōyō ga ichiban utsukushii.
examples.tr: When it comes to autumn, the fall leaves are the most beautiful after all.

pitfalls: It is not a real conditional. Do not use it for a result that follows from an action; use ～と or ～たら.
The second half is an association or general feeling, so commands and requests do not fit.
